title: Human Reproduction
seo_title: Grade 9 Natural Sciences: Human Reproduction Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: The male and female reproductive systems; puberty; the menstrual cycle; fertilisation, pregnancy and birth; contraception and the prevention of sexually transmitted infections, including HIV. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 9, Life and Living: Human reproduction)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): the reproductive organs, puberty, the menstrual cycle, fertilisation, pregnancy and birth. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Fertilisation is when a sperm joins an egg.
key_sub: The baby develops in the uterus.
body_html:
How to think about it

Sperm are made in the testes and pass through the sperm ducts and urethra. Eggs are made in the ovaries; each month an egg passes down the oviduct (fallopian tube). If a sperm meets the egg, fertilisation happens, and the fertilised egg implants in the uterus.

The menstrual cycle lasts about 28 days. During pregnancy (about 9 months) the baby gets food and oxygen through the placenta and umbilical cord. Abstinence and condoms prevent pregnancy and protect against sexually transmitted infections such as HIV.

Example

Where are eggs made?

Two small organs in the female

Answer: in the ovaries

Example

Where does fertilisation usually happen?

The tube from the ovary

Answer: in the oviduct

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up the uterus and the ovary.
  • Thinking menstruation is when the egg is released.
  • Thinking the mother's and baby's blood mix.

items.q: Is a condom a temporary or a permanent method of birth control?
items.e: It stops sperm from entering the vagina, and also reduces the spread of STIs.

It is cured by taking vitamins.
items.e: Bacterial STIs can be cured with antibiotics; viral STIs such as AIDS cannot.
